# v0.14.0 — security release

## ⚠️ Security advisory: two more quadratic paths in text shaping

**v0.13.0's fix for quadratic-time text shaping (GHSA-7jjg-q5vf-8592) was incomplete.** Re-testing with more base letters, scripts and fonts found two more independent O(n²) hot spots, both reachable with nothing more than ordinary caller-supplied text drawn through an embedded font:

- **GPOS mark attachment** — `propagateAttachment` summed every glyph's advance between a mark and its base on every call, so N combining marks on one base cost O(N²). The previous fix's own test used the base letter "a", which recomposes with U+0301 into "á" and never reaches this loop; other bases (x, Cyrillic и, Arabic ب, Hebrew ב) still did. Advances are now summed once per shaping run into a prefix array, and each mark's offset is one subtraction.
- **GSUB ligature and multiple substitution** — `ligate` and `gsubMultiple` spliced the whole remaining glyph buffer on every substitution, so a long line with a ligature every few characters (repeated "office ", anything a font turns into "fi"/"ffi") cost O(n²). Consumed glyphs are now marked in place and the buffer is rebuilt once per lookup, in one O(n) pass. A side effect, pinned by its own test: several back-to-back zero-length deletions used to remove only every other one; all of them are now removed.

Both are verified by randomized differential tests against the original implementations and by growth-ratio tests across several bases, scripts and a TrueType and a CFF font.

Also fixed in the same report (not a security issue): `Validate` still regex-scanned every stream's bytes for `N G R`-shaped text into a dependency map nothing read. Removed — about 11× faster on an image-heavy document.

Reported privately via GitHub's security advisory process by **shadowhunter1470-svg**. See the GitHub Security Advisory for the full write-up and affected-version details.

**All users should upgrade to v0.14.0.**

## Also in this release

New: **`TextStyle.MissingGlyph` / `ReplacementRune`** — an opt-in policy for a character the font has no glyph for, which `AddText`/`AddTextAt`/`MeasureText` otherwise draw silently as `.notdef`. `MissingGlyphError` fails the call and names the character; `MissingGlyphReplace` substitutes `ReplacementRune` (default U+FFFD). The zero value keeps the existing behavior. `ValidatePDFA`/`ConvertToPDFA` now also detect a used `.notdef` glyph, which PDF/A forbids.

GitHub issues fixed (both reported by **shadowhunter1470-svg**):

- **#19** — `AddText`/`AddTextAt`/`MeasureText`/`GetFontMetrics` accepted NaN/±Infinity coordinates, sizes, rotations and skews, writing text no PDF reader can parse into the content stream; they now return an error. `GetFontMetrics(nil, …)` now defaults to Helvetica like the other three.
- **#20** — drawing many shapes on one page or canvas was quadratic in the number of calls (now constant time per call); a rejected draw on a frozen `XForm`/`TilingPattern`/`Type3Font` canvas no longer leaves fonts, ExtGStates or glyph usage behind in the document; `AddTable` on a short canvas no longer fails when the table fits.

`ApplyRedactions` closes its last known gaps:

- A **tiling pattern** whose every fill was redacted away is now removed from the page's resources, so the content of its cell (which can include text) no longer stays in the saved file.
- A non-embedded font named by a **Standard-14 alias** (`/Arial`, `/TimesNewRoman`, `/CourierNew`, …) with no `/Encoding` is no longer refused by `ApplyRedactions`/`ReplaceText`, and its text now extracts instead of coming back as U+FFFD.
- A marked-content span left **open at the end of a malformed stream** has its `/ActualText` scrubbed like any other.

Rendering and memory:

- Text under **`0 Tz`** (zero horizontal scaling) now renders as zero-width, matching text extraction, pdf.js and MuPDF.
- Text extraction and redaction no longer copy the whole font description on every `q` operator (~17 KB → ~900 bytes allocated per operator on a stream of bare `q`s).

## Upgrading

No breaking API changes — `TextStyle.MissingGlyph`/`ReplacementRune` are additive and default to the previous behavior. Code that passed NaN or Infinity to the text functions now gets an error instead of a malformed PDF. Recompiling against v0.14.0 is sufficient to pick up the fixes.

## Full changelog

https://github.com/aspose-pdf-foss/aspose-pdf-foss-for-go/compare/v0.13.0...v0.14.0

# v0.13.0 — security release

## ⚠️ Security advisory: quadratic-time text shaping

**A long run of consecutive Unicode combining marks made text shaping with an embedded font quadratic in time.** `AddText` could be stalled for seconds by a text value of only a few kilobytes — plausible user input, such as combining diacritics typed instead of precomposed characters (a form field, a name, any string drawn through an embedded font).

Two independent O(n²) hot spots: `canonicalOrder` (the Unicode canonical-ordering pass OpenType shaping requires) was an insertion sort over each run of marks; `prevBase` (used by GPOS mark-attachment positioning to find the base glyph a mark attaches to) rescanned backward through every earlier mark on every call. `canonicalOrder` now sorts each run with a stable O(n log n) sort — provably identical output to the old algorithm, since a stable sort by the same total order is mathematically guaranteed to produce the same permutation. `prevBase` now answers from a cache built once per shaping run in a single forward O(n) pass. ~240× faster on the reporter's own reproduction (7.9s → ~33ms for 16,000 marks).

Reported privately via GitHub's security advisory process by **shadowhunter1470-svg**. See the GitHub Security Advisory for the full write-up and affected-version details.

## ⚠️ Security advisory: object references matched by regex against raw stream bytes

**`Extract`/`Split`, `Append`, and `RemoveUnusedObjects` treated digit sequences that happened to appear inside ordinary stream data as real object references.** `collectValueDepsDoc`, `markReachable` and `rewriteRefs` additionally regex-scanned a stream's own decoded data bytes — page text, font programs, images, compressed bytes — for anything shaped like an indirect reference (`N G R`) and treated every match as a real dependency, even though stream data is not PDF syntax and a content stream only ever names a resource by name through `/Resources`.

Three confirmed consequences, all closed by removing the scan entirely:

- **`Extract`/`Split`** could pull in a wholly unrelated object whenever a page's own text happened to contain a reference-shaped digit sequence — splitting a multi-party document one page per recipient could leak a *different* recipient's page content into a file meant to hold only one page.
- **`Append`** could silently rewrite the appended document's own visible text (or font/image binary data) whenever it happened to contain a sequence naming one of its own real objects, which then got renumbered mid-import.
- **`RemoveUnusedObjects`** could keep a genuinely dead object alive forever whenever its number coincidentally appeared inside an unrelated stream's bytes.

The identical pattern inside `Optimize`'s duplicate-stream merging (which reuses the same `rewriteRefs`) is closed by the same fix.

Reported privately via GitHub's security advisory process by **shadowhunter1470-svg**. See the GitHub Security Advisory for the full write-up and affected-version details.

**All users should upgrade to v0.13.0.**

## Also in this release

Continued hardening of `ApplyRedactions`:

- **Text rise (`Ts`)** is now tracked the same way character/word spacing are, including through `q`/`Q` and Form XObject inheritance — a redaction region drawn tightly around the *visible* (risen) position of a superscript/subscript glyph is no longer missed by a test point that stayed stuck at the baseline.
- A **non-Identity CJK CMap**'s Type0 text (e.g. `90ms-RKSJ-H`, or a PDF's own embedded `/Encoding` CMap stream) now decodes through the font's real codespace instead of assuming a fixed 2-byte stride, fixing misdecoded glyph boundaries that could drop the wrong text or leave a secret unredacted.
- A page's **`/Thumb` thumbnail** no longer survives a redaction untouched — it's dropped outright, since nothing in this library's own read path consults one and it could otherwise keep showing the pre-redaction page.
- A **Form XObject relying on an inherited font** (no `Tf` of its own, legal per ISO 32000-1 §8.10.1) can now be redacted instead of refused outright.
- **Byte-identical Form XObject placements are now memoized** instead of cloned again for every occurrence — a document placing one large, compressible form many times at the same spot no longer inflates the saved file with duplicate clones.

Two GitHub issues fixed (both reported by **shadowhunter1470-svg**):

- **#17** — Detached drawing canvases (`XForm.Canvas`, `TilingPattern.Canvas`, a `Type3Font` glyph canvas) no longer leak their own content-stream objects into the saved file, and drawing on one after it's been placed/used now errors instead of silently keeping the extra content. `Size()`, `MediaBox()`, and `AddTable()` now work on a detached canvas as documented, instead of failing with `"object 0 not found"`.
- **#18** — A new single-line text primitive for a caller that already does its own line-breaking and positioning: `(*Page).AddTextAt(text, style, x, y)` draws one line with no word-wrapping, no clipping, and whitespace kept exactly as given; `MeasureText` and `GetFontMetrics` let that caller measure text and font metrics the same way `AddText` draws them.

## Upgrading

No breaking API changes — `AddTextAt`/`MeasureText`/`GetFontMetrics` are additive. Existing code continues to work unchanged; recompiling against v0.13.0 is sufficient to pick up the fixes.

## Full changelog

https://github.com/aspose-pdf-foss/aspose-pdf-foss-for-go/compare/v0.12.0...v0.13.0

# v0.12.0 — security release

## ⚠️ Security advisory

**PDF names were written without escaping, so a caller-supplied string could inject arbitrary PDF syntax.** `writeValue` wrote every PDF name verbatim — both as a dictionary *value* and, critically, as a dictionary *key* — instead of escaping bytes outside the printable range plus `#` and the eight PDF delimiters (`( ) < > [ ] { } / %`) as ISO 32000-1 §7.3.5 requires. Where a name's bytes come from caller data — a `Document.Info` `Custom` map key, a font's `/BaseFont` read from a loaded font file's name table, a radio button's `Export` name — a delimiter or whitespace byte in that string ended the name early and the rest became further, unintended PDF syntax: a `Custom` key of `"Dept /Injected (yes) /X"` became *two* real dictionary entries in the saved file instead of one oddly-named one.

The identical bug existed independently in a second content-stream-operand serializer (used by redaction, grayscale conversion, and every other content-stream rewrite) and in inline-image dictionary keys. All three are fixed by one centralized `writeNameValue` helper; the reader now decodes the matching `#xx` escapes back, so a name that gets escaped on write round-trips to the original rather than to its own escaped text.

Reported privately through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting channel, with a precise reproduction, by **shadowhunter1470-svg** — thank you for the continued careful reports. See the GitHub Security Advisory for the full write-up and affected-version details.

**All users should upgrade to v0.12.0.**

## Also in this release

Continued hardening of `ApplyRedactions` after v0.11.0's stopgap:

- A redaction region overlapping a **Form XObject** is now actually redacted into instead of refused outright — the region is mapped into the form's own local content-stream space and the same three rewriters used at the page level run on its content, cloning only the specific placements that need a change so a Form XObject shared by other, untouched placements is never corrupted.
- Text drawn after a page-level coordinate transform (`cm`) — the common top-left-origin Y-flip many producers (Chrome/Skia included) emit once per page — could **escape redaction entirely**; the text rewriter now accounts for the active transform the same way the path and image rewriters already did.
- A `Tj`/`TJ` run under a font the pipeline couldn't resolve used to pass through **unredacted** while the call reported success; it now refuses with an error instead of silently leaving text recoverable.
- A marked-content span's stale `/ActualText` accessibility replacement is now scrubbed whenever anything inside the span was redacted, closing a path where `ExtractText`/`SearchText` could return the original secret text verbatim.
- Redaction now reaches **every other annotation's own appearance** — including a form Widget's own rendering of its field value (e.g. a visible SSN in a text field) — and drops/clips a small image embedded directly in the content stream (`BI`...`ID`...`EI`) the same way it already handled an Image XObject.

Four bugs reported via **GitHub issue #16** (shadowhunter1470-svg):

- Drawing on an already-rendered page no longer **duplicates the whole page's content** on every `AddText`/`Draw*`/`AddImage`/table-cell call — an append now adds one new entry to a `/Contents` array instead of decoding, concatenating, and rewriting the whole thing. This was the traced root cause behind the earlier `Optimize` slowdown (GitHub issue #9) and the `ApplyRedactions` content-leak fixed in v0.11.0.
- New content appended to a page no longer **inherits a leftover, unbalanced graphics state** (an unmatched `cm`, an active clip, invisible-text mode) left by whatever was drawn before it.
- The linearized ("fast web view") writer's `/ID` is now derived from actual document content instead of just object/page counts, so it no longer **collides two different documents** on the same file identifier, and an opened document keeps its own permanent `/ID` across re-linearization.
- Dictionary/array numeric values are now always written in plain decimal notation, never scientific notation (`-1e-13`) — a form this library's own parser (correctly implementing the no-exponent PDF number grammar) couldn't read back, silently losing the value on reopen.

One bug reported via **GitHub issue #14** (shadowhunter1470-svg):

- `AddText`'s word-wrapping now measures the real, **shaped** (kerned) width of a candidate line instead of the unshaped sum of character advances, so text no longer overflows its rectangle or wraps a line earlier than necessary with fonts that carry kerning/ligature tables.

## Upgrading

No API changes. Existing code continues to work unchanged; recompiling against v0.12.0 is sufficient to pick up the fixes.

## Full changelog

https://github.com/aspose-pdf-foss/aspose-pdf-foss-for-go/compare/v0.11.0...v0.12.0

# v0.11.0 — Security Release

**`ApplyRedactions` left redacted content fully recoverable in the saved file.** Reported privately through GitHub's new private vulnerability reporting channel, with a precise reproduction and root-cause analysis. Fixed, along with a related and more serious gap our own review of that fix uncovered. Also in this release: a one-call hidden-data sanitizer, and two community-reported bugs.

## Security: redacted content was recoverable

`ApplyRedactions` rewrites a redacted page's content stream and repoints `/Contents` at the new, clean stream — but the old one, still carrying the full pre-redaction text or image data, stayed in the saved file as an unreferenced object. The PDF writer has no reachability pass of its own, so it serialized that abandoned object anyway: recoverable with any PDF tool (`qpdf --show-object`, a stream dump, `/ToUnicode` on an embedded font) despite never appearing in `ExtractText` or on the rendered page.

- **Fixed**: `ApplyRedactions` now calls `RemoveUnusedObjects()` once at the end when it redacted at least one page, closing both of the reporter's reproductions in full.
- **A second, more serious gap, found during our own review of that fix**: a **Form XObject** intersecting a redaction region was never actually redacted at all — our pipeline treated it like an Image XObject (drop the `Do` invocation if fully covered), but a Form XObject can itself hold arbitrary text, and nothing in the pipeline recurses into one. Reachable through this library's own public `AddForm` API, and by extension `NUp`/`Booklet`/`PdfPageStamp`.
- **Fixed as a safety stopgap, not yet the real fix**: `ApplyRedactions` and `ValidateRedactions` now refuse outright (an error) when a redaction region intersects a Form XObject, rather than silently succeeding. Getting this check itself right took two further rounds of review: the geometry math needs a Form XObject's own `/BBox`+`/Matrix`, not the unit square an Image XObject always uses, and a Form with an unresolvable `/BBox` must be treated as unsafe outright rather than guessed at.
- **Known limitations, documented and tracked, not hidden**: a fully-covered image XObject's `/Resources/XObject` entry stays reachable (its pixel data survives, lower severity than text); a page's `/Thumb` thumbnail is never touched; redacting a document later saved incrementally (already signed, or with validation info) keeps the original text in the earlier, byte-preserved revision by design; redacting a Form XObject's own content remains unsupported (now a clear error instead of a silent gap).

A GitHub Security Advisory has the full writeup, affected versions, and credit to the reporter.

## Also in this release

- **`Document.Sanitize`** — `HiddenDataSanitizationOptions` composes metadata, attachment, script, annotation, layer and form removal, plus optional page rasterization, into one call — mirroring Aspose.PDF for .NET's `HiddenDataSanitizer`. `AllHiddenDataSanitizationOptions()` mirrors the static `.All()` preset.
- **`ConvertToPDFA` fixed**: a Standard-14 font substitute was flagged Symbolic when ISO 32000-1 requires Nonsymbolic for a simple TrueType font carrying `/Encoding` — veraPDF failed the file even though our own validator reported it conformant. Verified against actual veraPDF 1.30.3, before and after.
- **`SetInfo` fixed**: non-ASCII metadata values were written as raw UTF-8 instead of a proper PDF text string (PDFDocEncoding or UTF-16BE with a byte-order mark), so umlauts and other non-ASCII characters came back garbled in `pdfinfo` and other readers.

## Upgrading

No breaking changes for ordinary use. `ApplyRedactions`/`ValidateRedactions` can now return an error for a redaction region that intersects a Form XObject — a case that previously succeeded silently while leaving the content recoverable. If you see this error, the fix is to flatten the Form XObject into page content first, or keep redaction regions clear of it; redacting a Form XObject's own content is tracked for a future release.

```
go get github.com/aspose-pdf-foss/aspose-pdf-foss-for-go@v0.11.0
```

# v0.10.0 — Long-Term Validation and Object Streams

Signatures gain long-term validation: revocation checking over OCSP or a CRL, and a document that carries its own certificates and revocation evidence so a signature keeps validating years after the certificate expires. The document comparison epic completes with graphical (pixel) comparison, vector side-by-side spreads, and four diff output generators. Object streams join `Optimize`'s default lossless preset. E-invoices round out PDF/A-3's associated-files story. And three bugs reported by the community against v0.9.0 are fixed, alongside two externally contributed pull requests. Pure Go, zero dependencies, as always.

## Signature revocation checking and LTV

`VerifySignatures`/`VerifySignature` take `ValidationOptions{Revocation, Fetcher, Timeout}`:

- **`RevocationOffline`** checks only material the document already carries (its `/DSS`); **`RevocationOnline`** also fetches from the certificate's OCSP responders and CRL distribution points.
- OCSP and CRL are hand-rolled on `encoding/asn1`, like the rest of the CMS stack — no dependency. A response counts only when signed by the issuer or a delegated OCSP-signing responder; a stale or mismatched answer is reported `Unknown`, never a comfortable "good".
- `SignatureVerification.Revocation` reports status, source, revocation time and reason. **`Valid` keeps its cryptographic meaning throughout** — a revoked certificate never flips it.
- `Document.AddValidationInfo` writes the certificates and revocation material into the catalog as a `/DSS` with per-signature `/VRI`, appended as a new revision so existing signatures stay valid — the document now carries its own long-term evidence. `SignOptions.LTV` does this automatically right after signing.

## Object streams (`OptimizationOptions.CompressObjects`)

Now part of `DefaultOptimizationOptions()`: packs every non-stream object into Flate-compressed object streams and writes a cross-reference stream instead of the classic xref table. Lossless, **21.6% smaller** across the test corpus; encrypted and signed documents round-trip, and a later incremental revision keeps the file's cross-reference kind so earlier signatures stay valid. PDF/A-1 is exempt (it predates object streams).

## Document comparison epic completes

- **Graphical comparison** (`GraphicalPdfComparer.GetDifference`) rasterizes two pages and diffs pixels — for changes word-diffing can't see: moved or edited graphics, font substitution, a replaced scanned image. A `Threshold` percentage ignores recompression noise and anti-aliasing.
- **Side-by-side spreads** (`SideBySideComparePages`/`SideBySideCompareDocuments`) lay the marked-up before and after next to each other in one PDF — built on the existing word-diff and markup machinery, so unlike a rasterized picture the spread stays **vector**.
- **Four diff output generators** — HTML (a colored fragment for embedding), JSON, GFM Markdown, and a generated, word-wrapped PDF report — serialize a comparison's `DiffOperation`s, mirroring Aspose.PDF for .NET's `OutputGenerator` namespace.

## E-invoices: ZUGFeRD / Factur-X

`Document.AttachInvoice(xml, InvoiceOptions{...})` packages a Cross Industry Invoice as a hybrid e-invoice — embedded with the relationship its profile requires, described by `fx:` XMP properties and the matching PDF/A extension schema, converted to PDF/A-3. `Document.Invoice()` reads it back from Factur-X 1.0, ZUGFeRD 2.1+, 2.0 and 1.0 files. Checked against the `factur-x` reference library, including its official XSD.

## Also in this release

- **Signing without holding the key** (`SignOptions.SignHash`) — a callback returns the signature for a hardware module or remote signing service.
- **Per-signature verification** — `SignatureNames()` and `VerifySignature(fieldName)`, plus the signer's embedded certificate chain.
- **SHA-3 signatures** — `SignOptions.Digest` adds SHA-384/512 and the SHA-3 family alongside the SHA-256 default.
- **Reading AES-256 revision 5** — the withdrawn Adobe Extension Level 3 scheme now opens.
- **`ConvertToPDFA` flattens transparency for PDF/A-1** automatically, closing the last manual step for that format.
- **`Optimize.UnembedFonts`** (opt-in) drops a font program that's metric-compatible with a Standard-14 face, relying on the renderer's substitution instead.
- **`FileAttachmentAnnotation.AFRelationship`** — page-pinned attachments get the same PDF/A-3 association a document-level `EmbeddedFile` already had.
- **Layout-preserving text extraction** (`TextExtractFlatten`) — a page comes back on a fixed-pitch grid, so a ruled table's columns stay aligned and two revisions diff cleanly.
- **RC4-40 encryption** for old readers and archives (with a loud warning that it's breakable in minutes).
- **Damage reporting** — `NeedsRepair()`/`RepairReport()` say whether a file had to be recovered to open, instead of repairing silently.
- **Tagged PDF: annotations in the structure tree** — `StructElement.AddObjectReference` ties a structure element to an annotation via `/OBJR`, the mechanism a `/Link` element uses to point at its `LinkAnnotation`.

## Fixed

Three bugs reported against v0.9.0 by the community, all with thanks to the reporter:

- **PDF/A documents saved with `WriteTo` had no trailer `/ID`** — PDF/A requires one unconditionally (ISO 19005-2 §6.1.3); veraPDF reported `6.1.3-1`. Fixed, with regression tests. (issue #11)
- **`RemoveUnusedObjects` deleted content reachable only from the catalog** — the default `Optimize` preset dropped XMP metadata, tagged-PDF structure, embedded files, JavaScript, unused layers, output intents and unloaded bookmarks, since the catalog wasn't itself a reachability root. Already fixed on `main` by the time this was filed; the issue's exact repros now have regression tests pinning them. (issue #10)
- **`Optimize` was up to ~25x slower than necessary** on documents built from many small `AddText` calls — a `RemoveUnusedObjects` pre-pass now clears dead content-stream copies before the other transforms waste time scanning them. (issue #9)

Two externally contributed pull requests, merged:

- **A wrong password no longer opens a cross-reference-stream encrypted PDF** — `OpenWithPassword` silently accepted any password and handed back still-encrypted content for files whose only cross-reference section is an xref stream. A rejected password now ends the open, reported via the new `ErrInvalidPassword` sentinel.
- **A `/Pages` node with an indirect `/Kids` reference no longer produces a zero-page document** — ISO 32000-1 §7.3.10 permits an indirect `/Kids`/`/Count`, which page trees from Oracle Reports use; the walker now resolves the reference.

Also: `RemoveDuplicateStreams`/`CompressStreams` deleted `removeDuplicateStreams`; re-saving an RC4-40 or AES-256 encrypted document kept the wrong security handler or header; incremental revisions (a second signature, `AddValidationInfo`) dropped `/Info`; several XMP extension-schema and prefix-collision bugs around `ConvertToPDFA`; `SearchText` match rectangles now cover descenders instead of starting at the baseline.

## Upgrading

No breaking changes: every v0.9.0 call compiles and behaves the same, except `SearchText`/markup-annotation callers that relied on `Rect.LLY` being the text baseline — it is now the descender, the convention viewers expect for highlight and redaction quads. Read the baseline from `ExtractTextWithLayout` instead if needed.

```
go get github.com/aspose-pdf-foss/aspose-pdf-foss-for-go@v0.10.0
```

# v0.9.0 — Complex Scripts and Document Comparison

Two headline capabilities, both pure Go with zero dependencies: text is now **shaped by the font's own OpenType tables**, and two PDFs can be **compared word by word** — with the differences drawn back onto the document, not just listed. Alongside them, right-to-left text extracts in reading order at last, PDF/A conversion closes its font and appearance gaps, and text-markup annotations draw themselves.

## OpenType shaping (GSUB/GPOS)

Text drawn with an embedded OpenType font is shaped by the font's own layout tables. No API change — `AddText` simply gets it right.

- **Arabic, Persian and Urdu join properly.** A font is no longer required to carry Presentation Forms-B: Amiri, Noto Naskh and most modern Arabic faces shape through their own contextual forms, so the script renders connected instead of as isolated letters. Joining classes come from the Unicode `ArabicShaping` data, so Syriac and N'Ko join too.
- **Marks land where they belong.** Harakat and Hebrew points attach to their base letters through GPOS mark and mark-to-mark attachment, including shadda-plus-fatha stacks and the dagesh-before-vowel ordering HarfBuzz uses.
- **Ligatures and kerning** apply from the font's own lookups.
- **Glyph-for-glyph identical to HarfBuzz** on a 54-string Arabic/Persian/Urdu/Hebrew/Latin differential suite across DejaVu Sans, Amiri, Noto Naskh and Noto Sans Arabic; MuPDF renders our output exactly as our own renderer does.
- **Shaped text stays extractable and searchable.** A substituted glyph claims its characters through `/ToUnicode`; clusters no single glyph can name (a lam-alef ligature, a decomposition piece, a hidden joiner) carry `/ActualText`.
- The engine reads GDEF, GSUB types 1–8 and GPOS types 1–9 — contextual, chaining, cursive and mark attachment included — defensively: a malformed subtable is dropped, never fatal. Unkerned text still produces byte-identical content streams, so nothing regressed for Latin.

Out of scope, as before: the Indic/Khmer/Myanmar/Hangul reordering shapers, vertical text, variation tables.

## Document comparison (`CompareDocumentsPageByPage`, `CompareFlatDocuments`, `ComparePages`)

A new subsystem mirroring the text half of Aspose.PDF for .NET's `Aspose.Pdf.Comparison` — `TextPdfComparer`, `DiffOperation`, `ComparisonOptions`.

- **Word-level diff** over Myers, with the common prefix and suffix trimmed first. Page-by-page pairs pages by index; flat mode treats each document as one continuous text, so content that moved across a page break reads as unchanged.
- **Every difference knows where it is.** Aspose's `DiffOperation` carries an operation and its text; ours also carries the page and the rectangles the run occupies on *both* sides. That is what makes the next point possible.
- **A marked-up copy, not just a report.** `ComparisonResult.SaveMarkup` writes a copy of either document with insertions highlighted and deletions struck out (or, on the new document, a caret carrying the removed text), every annotation titled so a viewer's comments panel reads as the change list. The input documents are never mutated.
- **Right-to-left aware**: words come from the layout extractor through the same rune-map machinery `SearchText` uses, so Arabic and Hebrew compare in logical order and the rectangles still land on the right glyphs.
- `ComparisonOptions` mirrors theirs — `ExtractionArea`, `ExcludeAreas1/2`, `ExcludeTables` (through the `TableAbsorber`), `EditOperationsOrder` — and adds `IgnoreCase`. `AssembleSourceText`/`AssembleDestinationText` rebuild either side from the operations.
- Corpus: every one of 1,008 documents compared against itself reports no differences, in 14 seconds.

Graphical (pixel) comparison, the side-by-side spread and the HTML/JSON/Markdown diff generators are the next phases.

## Fixed

- **Right-to-left text extracts in reading order.** Arabic and Hebrew glyphs sit on the page in visual order and `ExtractText` returned them that way, so every word read backwards and a copied line was unusable. Lines carrying right-to-left characters are now put back into the order their characters were typed, which also makes `SearchText` match a phrase as it is typed. `TextExtractRaw` keeps content-stream order by design.
- **PDF/A conversion closes its font and appearance gaps.** `ConvertToPDFA` draws the appearances annotations are missing (form-field widgets included — a conforming reader may not synthesize one, so a checkbox without it simply vanished), embeds composite CJK fonts as a glyph subset of the matching installed face, and embeds Symbol or ZapfDingbats from a registered face. Embedding permissions are honoured throughout: a face whose OS/2 `fsType` forbids embedding is never written into a document. Corpus: documents converting to a clean report went from **766 to 971** of 1,003.
- **PDF/A no longer reports fonts nothing draws with.** Only the fonts a content stream actually selects with `Tf` are checked, as ISO 19005-1 requires and veraPDF reports — an Acrobat form keeps ZapfDingbats in `/AcroForm/DR` whether or not anything draws with it, and 130 corpus documents were failed for exactly that.

Each type now generates its own, regenerated by `SetQuadPoints`/`SetColor`/`SetRect`, and the renderer synthesizes one for an `/AP`-less markup annotation parsed from another producer's file.
- **Ligatures extract as all of their letters.** A `/ToUnicode` entry mapping one glyph to several characters (the "fi" ligature common in LaTeX and Word output) extracted as its first character only, and a supplementary-plane destination as nothing. Both read back whole now.
- **Embedded fonts write a deterministic `/ToUnicode`.** A glyph shared by two characters (the space glyph usually serves U+00A0 too) was written with both mappings in random order, so a space could extract as a no-break space from one save to the next. Each glyph now maps to its lowest code point.

# v0.8.1 — Encrypted-stream data loss

A single fix, recommended for everyone reading or writing encrypted PDFs.

## Fixed: an encrypted stream could be silently destroyed on read

Roughly **one encrypted stream in 500** was lost while the document was being parsed.

The parser decodes a stream's declared `/Filter` as it reads it, on the assumption that ciphertext never survives its filter. That assumption is false: a zlib header is only *"CM == 8 and (CMF<<8|FLG) % 31 == 0"*, which random ciphertext satisfies about that often, and the Flate decoder's deliberate tolerance of a truncated tail then returns a byte or two of garbage instead of an error. The stream was marked decoded, the decryption pass skipped it as already-clean, and its real content was gone.

The damage was quiet and content-dependent. In the case that exposed it, a font's `/ToUnicode` CMap collapsed to a single byte, so one space in the extracted text came back as U+FFFD — visible only as an intermittent test failure that never reproduced on a rerun.

Streams are now always decrypted from the bytes exactly as they appear in the file, with the streams a conforming producer leaves in the clear correctly exempt: cross-reference streams (never encrypted, ISO 32000-1 §7.5.8.2) and the metadata stream when `/EncryptMetadata` is false.

**Verification**: reproduced first (2 failures in 500 encrypt/reopen cycles), then a corpus sweep of **1,009 documents** encrypting, reopening and extracting byte-identical text under RC4-128, AES-128 and AES-256, plus regression tests that fail against the old behaviour.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/aspose-pdf-foss/aspose-pdf-foss-for-go/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

# v0.8.0 — Spreadsheets, Colour and Closed Workflows

Five additions, all pure Go with zero dependencies: PDF converts to **Excel workbooks**, ICCBased colour finally goes **through the embedded profile**, documents can be encrypted for **certificate recipients** instead of a password, attachments can be presented as a **portfolio**, and custom glyphs can be **authored as a Type3 font**.

## PDF → XLSX (`Document.SaveXlsx`)

Detected tables (ruled or borderless) become Excel worksheets — built on the `TableAbsorber`, mirroring Aspose.PDF for .NET's `SaveFormat.Excel` + `ExcelSaveOptions`.

- **Numbers are numbers.** Plain values under either separator convention (`1 234,56` / `1,234.56`), percentages and single-symbol currency amounts land as numeric cells with matching number formats — `SUM()` over an exported column works immediately (Excel-verified: the showcase restaurant bill sums to 133,00 €).
- **Multi-page tables stitched.** Tables continuing across consecutive pages with the same column signature merge into one sheet with the repeated header dropped — a 2-page 41+21-row table arrives as a single 62-row block.
- **Structure and styling carry over**: merged cells (`RowSpan`/`ColSpan` → `mergeCells`), header shading, bold/colour, per-column alignment and widths.
- **Two modes**: `XlsxTablesOnly` (default — every table stacked on one worksheet with page captions) and `XlsxFullPage` (a worksheet per page carrying all text laid into cells, plus the page's images as anchored pictures).
- Output is strict-ECMA-376-valid SpreadsheetML. Corpus: 1,014/1,014 documents convert panic-free and validate; Excel opens every smoke workbook without repair.

## ICC colour management

ICCBased colour spaces are converted through their embedded profile instead of being passed through as the underlying device space, so wide-gamut sources (AdobeRGB and friends) no longer render oversaturated.

- Pure-Go ICC v2 parser and transform engine: matrix/TRC RGB and grayscale-TRC profiles (`curv` and parametric `para` tone curves) plus lut8/lut16 CLUT pipelines with XYZ or Lab connection space; PCS → sRGB through the Bradford-adapted D50→D65 matrix.
- Wired into both image extraction and the renderer's colour operators.
- **sRGB-likeness detection** keeps the overwhelmingly common case free: in the 1,000+ document corpus, 93 of 106 embedded RGB profiles short-circuit, and all 156 profiles parse.
- No lcms, no cgo.

## Certificate-based encryption (public-key security handler)

`EncryptionOptions.Recipients` seals a document for a list of X.509 certificates instead of a shared password (`/Filter /Adobe.PubSec`, AES-128 or AES-256), and `OpenWithCertificate`/`OpenStreamWithCertificate` open it with the recipient's certificate and any `crypto.Decrypter` private key — no `.p12` file, matching how `Sign` already takes a `crypto.Signer`.

- **Per-recipient permissions**: each recipient's envelope carries its own permission set, something a shared password cannot express.
- Editing a certificate-encrypted document re-saves it for the same recipients.
- The CMS EnvelopedData envelopes are hand-rolled on `encoding/asn1` beside the existing signing code and cross-verified with **OpenSSL** (`cms -decrypt` recovers the payload byte-for-byte).
- RSA recipients (PKCS#1 v1.5 key transport); EC key agreement and the legacy RC4 sub-filters are out of scope.

## PDF portfolios

`Document.Collection()` presents the document's embedded files as a portfolio rather than a plain attachment list: a schema of viewer columns (`Schema().Add("Amount", "Total", CollectionFieldNumber)` — text, number and date columns, plus filename/description/dates/size derived from the attachment itself), per-file values through `EmbeddedFile.CollectionItem()`, an initial file, a sort field, and a details/tiles/hidden presentation mode. `Remove()` reverts to an ordinary attachment list without touching the files, and the cover page still opens in viewers that ignore portfolios. Verified with pikepdf on a generated three-invoice portfolio.

## Type3 font authoring (beyond Aspose)

`Document.CreateType3Font()` + `Type3Font.AddGlyph(rune, width)` turn the vector drawing API into a font factory: each glyph is a canvas in em space (1000 units, baseline at y=0) that accepts paths, gradients, even images, and the finished font drops into `TextStyle.Font` next to any other face. The font embeds uniXXXX glyph names and a ToUnicode CMap, so text drawn with custom symbols still extracts, searches and renders. Aspose.PDF for .NET exposes no equivalent.

## Fixed

- **Converters no longer embed decompression-bomb images.** A degenerate PDF can declare a gigapixel image from a few KB of flate (a corpus file carries 35000×35000 in an 11 KB document); the converters embedded the decoded raster verbatim, producing a DOCX that crashed LibreOffice and stalled Word. Rasters above 30 megapixels are now skipped at collection time.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/aspose-pdf-foss/aspose-pdf-foss-for-go/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

# Aspose.PDF FOSS for Go v0.6.0 — the AI & Markdown release

**Date:** 2026-07-21 · **Tag:** `v0.6.0` · 13 commits since v0.5.0 · pure Go, stdlib only, MIT.

## Headline

Two new engines. The **`ai` subpackage** brings AI copilots — summarize, OCR, chat, describe — over any **OpenAI-compatible** endpoint, with two capabilities Aspose.PDF for .NET doesn't have. The **Markdown → PDF renderer** turns CommonMark + GFM into cleanly typeset, paginated PDFs, backed by a parser that passes the official CommonMark test suite **652/652**.

## AI copilots (`ai` subpackage)

Mirrors the copilot layer of Aspose.PDF for .NET's `Aspose.Pdf.AI` — on the Go standard library alone. One client works with OpenAI, LiteLLM, Ollama, OpenRouter, or anything else speaking the chat-completions protocol; local endpoints are first-class, and nothing is ever sent unless a copilot is explicitly invoked.

| Copilot | What it does |
|---|---|
| `SummaryCopilot` | summarize (map-reduce over long docs) → text, PDF document, or file; `Markdown: true` renders a **formatted** summary |
| `OcrCopilot` | recognize scanned pages (auto-detected) via a vision model or any custom `OCREngine` (Tesseract, cloud) |
| `ChatCopilot` | document Q&A with conversation memory, grounded in the extracted text |
| `ImageDescriptionCopilot` | describe images / generate alt-text |

**Beyond Aspose:**

- **`MakeSearchable`** — OCRs a scanned PDF and writes the text back as an *invisible layer*: the file looks pixel-identical (asserted by tests) but becomes selectable, copyable and Ctrl+F-searchable. Aspose's OCR copilot only extracts text.
- **`FillAltTexts`** — walks a tagged PDF's structure tree, locates each figure's image through its marked-content MCID, describes it, and fills the missing `/Alt` — `ValidatePDFUA`'s `UA_FIGURE_NO_ALT` findings clear in one call.

New core primitives along the way: `TextStyle.Invisible` (text rendering mode 3) and `Document.FiguresNeedingAltText()`.

## Markdown → PDF

```go
doc, _ := pdf.MarkdownToDocument("report.md")   // mirrors Aspose's MdLoadOptions
doc.Save("report.pdf")
```

- **Provable conformance**: the pure-Go CommonMark parser passes the official 0.31.2 suite **652/652** (all 132 emphasis cases), asserted in CI; GFM tables, strikethrough, task lists and autolinks ride the same machinery.
- **One good-looking default theme**: scaled headings, real bold/italic/strike/code runs, links as clickable annotations, nested lists with drawn task checkboxes, block quotes with a rule, code blocks that keep their indentation, aligned GFM tables with repeating headers, images, automatic pagination.
- **Three entry points**: `MarkdownToDocument`/`FromStream`, `Flow.AddMarkdown` (mix into a flow), `Page.AddMarkdown(md, rect)`.
- **Accessible output**: `Tagged: true` builds the structure tree, title and language — passes the PDF/UA validator.
- **Full Unicode**: `FontFamily`/`CodeFontFamily` embed installed families (e.g. Arial/Consolas) for Cyrillic and beyond.
- The styled-runs paragraph layouter built for this (mixed styles, cross-run word wrap, shared baselines, link rects) is the foundation for a future HTML-lite importer.

## Unified optimizer

`Document.Optimize(OptimizationOptions)` runs remove-unused-objects, font subsetting, **lossless stream compression** (uncompressed source streams get Flate), **duplicate-stream deduplication** (byte-identical streams merged, all references repointed) and optional image recompression in one call, returning per-operation counts. `DefaultOptimizationOptions()` is the safe lossless preset — verified pixel-identical before/after. Mirrors `Document.OptimizeResources`.

## Quick start

```go
// AI: make a scan searchable with a local model.
client := ai.NewOpenAIClient(ai.OpenAIClientOptions{
    BaseURL: "http://localhost:11434/v1", Model: "llama3.2-vision",
})
scan, _ := pdf.Open("scanned.pdf")
ocr := ai.NewOcrCopilot(ai.NewLLMOCREngine(client, ai.LLMOCROptions{}), ai.OcrOptions{Document: scan})
n, _ := ocr.MakeSearchable(ctx)
_ = scan.Save("searchable.pdf")

// Markdown report with Cyrillic + formatted AI summary.
doc, _ := pdf.MarkdownToDocument("otchet.md", pdf.MarkdownOptions{FontFamily: "Arial"})
sum := ai.NewSummaryCopilot(client, ai.SummaryOptions{Document: doc, Markdown: true})
_ = sum.SaveSummary(ctx, "summary.pdf")
```

## Compatibility

No breaking changes. Everything remains pure Go, standard library only. The `ai` subpackage is opt-in — the root package stays free of AI and network code.

# Aspose.PDF FOSS for Go v0.5.0 — the HTML release

**Date:** 2026-07-09 · **Tag:** `v0.5.0` · 17 commits since v0.4.0 · pure Go, stdlib only, MIT.

## Headline

A complete **PDF → HTML converter** — the only one in the Go ecosystem, and in several ways ahead of Aspose.PDF for .NET and pdf2htmlEX. One entry point (`Document.SaveHTML` / `WriteHTML`), self-contained output, **zero JavaScript**.

## Four export modes

| Mode | What it is | When |
|---|---|---|
| `HTMLModeFaithful` (default) | Full page raster + transparent selectable text layer — pixel-identical to the PDF | maximum fidelity |
| `HTMLModeText` | Glyph-less background raster + real styled HTML text in the document's own fonts (WOFF) | reports, articles; ~half the size |
| `HTMLModeNative` | No raster at all: pages are inline SVG (true Bézier curves, native strokes, clips, `mix-blend-mode`), images keep their original JPEG/PNG bytes; only shadings/patterns/soft masks degrade to small positioned patches | web publishing, infinite zoom |
| `HTMLModeFlow` | Reflowable responsive article — paragraphs/headings inferred and re-assembled in reading order, rewraps on mobile | e-book-style reading |

## Interactive forms — the differentiator

`InteractiveForms: true` converts AcroForm fields into **real fillable HTML controls**: text/password/multiline, checkboxes, radio groups, combo/list boxes, typed `number`/`date` inputs (format-mask → ISO conversion), working **submit/reset buttons** inside a document-level `<form>`, PDF tab order, `FieldStyle` → CSS. Fill in, submit, print — no JavaScript. Aspose renders fields as static pictures; pdf2htmlEX too.

New public API on the way: `(*ButtonField).Action()/SetAction()` — push buttons can finally carry activation actions; `ButtonAppearance` colours now persist in `/MK`/`/DA` per spec.

## Fonts: WOFF embedding

Embedded TrueType/OpenType programs are re-wrapped as WOFF1 `@font-face` (pure Go: per-table zlib, synthesized browser `cmap` from `/ToUnicode` ∘ `/CIDToGIDMap`, minimal `name`/`OS∕2`/`post` for the OTS sanitizers). Text renders in the document's real faces; non-embeddable fonts fall back to metric substitutes width-fitted with `letter-spacing`/`scaleX`.

## Publishing toolkit

- **Outline sidebar** (`OutlineNav`) — the bookmark tree as a collapsible panel with a pure-CSS toggle button.
- **Multi-file output** — `ResourceWriter` callback (S3/CDN/anywhere) or `ResourceDir` (files next to the HTML); `SplitPages` writes one HTML per page with cross-file links. Showcase: 2.86 MB inline → 252 KB HTML + shared assets.
- **Asset deduplication** — byte-identical resources (repeated logos, table-header images, identical WOFFs) written once, keyed by SHA-256 of the final bytes; showcase assets: 127 files → 28.
- Link annotations → `<a>` overlays; `Pages` subsets; `loading="lazy"` backgrounds.

## Renderer

Transparency-group compositing (ISO 32000-1 §11.4.7): isolated groups render off-screen and composite once — fixing double-darkening under group alpha; knockout groups (`/K true`) supported. The renderer also drives the native SVG mode via a new vector backend with per-element raster degradation.

## Quick start

```go
doc, _ := pdf.Open("invoice.pdf")

// Crisp selectable preview (great replacement for JPEG page previews):
doc.SaveHTML("preview.html", pdf.HTMLSaveOptions{Mode: pdf.HTMLModeText})

// A browsable multi-page site with bookmarks and fillable forms:
doc.SaveHTML("site/doc.html", pdf.HTMLSaveOptions{
    Mode: pdf.HTMLModeNative, InteractiveForms: true,
    OutlineNav: true, ResourceDir: "assets", SplitPages: true,
})
```

## Fixed

- `Document.Save` no longer ignores the output file's `Close` error (possible silent data loss on full disks / flush failures).

## Compatibility

No breaking changes. Everything remains pure Go, standard library only.

Building on the v0.3.0 renderer, this release adds an enterprise and compliance layer, plus a document-generation and international-text stack — all still pure Go, standard library only, MIT-licensed. Headlines: **digital signatures** (sign/verify, PAdES, DocMDP certification, RFC 3161 timestamps, multiple signatures, and signing encrypted documents); the **PDF/A** + **PDF/UA** compliance stack (validate + convert across PDF/A-1/2/3 a/b with automatic font embedding and a pure-Go sRGB OutputIntent; a PDF/UA validator; and a **Tagged-PDF authoring** toolkit for accessible output); a **flow / document-generator** layout model (paragraphs, headings, tables, lists, floating boxes, multi-column, text flow-around, auto-pagination, optional auto-tagging); **right-to-left text** (a pure-Go Unicode BiDi engine with Arabic contextual shaping); a complete **AcroForm data-interchange** story (typed JSON, FDF, XFDF) with the extra field types (Number/Date/Password/RichText/FileSelect); **structural text extraction** (`ParagraphAbsorber`); and a batch of production helpers — reusable Form XObjects, tiling patterns, inline images, optional-content layers, document-level embedded files, linearized fast-web-view output, whole-document grayscale, and a PDF-page stamp. # Aspose.PDF FOSS for Go — v0.3.0

The headline of this release is a complete, **dependency-free page renderer**: PDF
pages rasterize to PNG / JPEG / GIF / BMP and single- or multi-page TIFF, covering
vector graphics, images, text, shadings, patterns, transparency, and annotation
appearances — all in pure Go, with no external dependencies. Months of visual
testing against a real-world PDF corpus drove a large batch of parsing and
rendering correctness/robustness fixes (78 in total). The release also adds page
flattening, full-text search, page deletion, and direct page-box setters.

No breaking changes since v0.2.0 beyond two API renames (see **Breaking changes**).

## Highlights

- **Render to image** — `Page.RenderImage` / `RenderPNG` / `RenderJPEG` / `RenderGIF`
  / `RenderBMP` / `RenderTIFF`, plus `Document.RenderTIFF` for a whole document and
  Aspose-style `Resolution` + `PngDevice` / `JpegDevice` / `GifDevice` / `BmpDevice`
  / `TiffDevice`. Pure Go, 150 DPI default, renders the CropBox.
- **Flatten** — bake form fields and annotations into static page content.
- **Search** — `Page.SearchText` / `Document.SearchText` with literal,
  case-insensitive, and RE2-regex modes; each match carries a bounding rectangle.
- **Robustness** — malformed real-world PDFs open and render instead of hanging,
  crashing, or blanking.

## Added — public API

- `(*Page).RenderImage(RenderOptions) (image.Image, error)` and
  `RenderPNG` / `RenderJPEG(…, quality)` / `RenderGIF` / `RenderBMP` / `RenderTIFF`
  encoders; `(*Document).RenderImage(pageNum, …)` and `(*Document).RenderTIFF(w, opts, pageNums…)`.
- Aspose-style device wrappers: `NewResolution(dpi)`, `PngDevice` / `JpegDevice` /
  `GifDevice` / `BmpDevice` (`Process(page, w)`), `TiffDevice`
  (`Process` + `ProcessDocument`).
- `FontRepository`: `AddFontFolder` / `AddFontFile` / `AddSystemFonts` /
  `ClearFontSources` — register fonts the renderer uses for non-embedded text.
- `(*Document).Flatten()` / `(*Form).Flatten()` / `(Field).Flatten()` /
  `(Annotation).Flatten()` / `(*AnnotationCollection).Flatten()`.
- `(*Page).SearchText(query, opts…)` / `(*Document).SearchText(query, opts…)` with
  `SearchOptions{CaseInsensitive, Regex}` and the `TextMatch` result type.
- `(*Document).DeletePage(n)` / `DeletePages(pageNums…)`.
- Page-box setters `(*Page).SetMediaBox/SetCropBox/SetTrimBox/SetBleedBox/SetArtBox(Rectangle)`,
  `(*Page).SetPageSize(width, height)`, and the new `(*Page).MediaBox()` getter.

## Renderer capability matrix

The renderer is implemented in six phases (P1–P6) plus annotations and TIFF. What
it draws today:

### Vector & colour
- Paths, fills, strokes; line caps / joins / dash patterns; miter-limit fallback.
- DeviceGray / DeviceRGB / DeviceCMYK, plus **Separation** and **DeviceN** colour
  with **Type 4 PostScript** tint transforms.
- Adobe-profile **DeviceCMYK → RGB** LUT so process colours match Acrobat.
- Axial (Type 2) and radial (Type 3) **shadings** via `sh` and shading patterns;
  **tiling patterns** (PatternType 1).
- **Clipping** (`W` / `W*`), **constant alpha** (`/ca` / `/CA`), **soft masks**
  (`/SMask` luminosity & alpha groups), separable and non-separable **blend modes**,
  and **Optional-Content** (OCG/OCMD) layer visibility.

### Images
- Image XObjects with `/SMask` alpha, stencil **image masks** (`/ImageMask`), and
  inline images (`BI`/`ID`/`EI`).
- Pure-Go codecs: **CCITTFaxDecode** (Group 4 / Group 3 1-D), **JBIG2** bilevel
  scans (arithmetic path: symbol-dictionary / text-region + generic / refinement;
  Huffman / MMR / halftone in phase 2), **JPEG2000** (`/JPXDecode`, incl. MRC
  high-resolution stencil-masked foreground layers), and the **LZWDecode** filter.
- Box-average minification for smooth downscaling and correct `/Matte` borders.

### Text
- Embedded **TrueType** (`/FontFile2`, own `glyf` decoder), **CFF / Type2**
  (`/FontFile3`: Type1C simple and CID-keyed, OpenType-CFF), classic **Type1**
  (`/FontFile`, in-house eexec + charstring interpreter), and **Type3**
  (`/CharProcs` content streams).
- Non-embedded fonts via bundled metric-compatible substitutes
  (Arimo / Tinos / Cousine / Carlito) and a `FontRepository` for exact and installed
  fonts (including `.ttc` collections and `.otf`/CFF).
- **Non-embedded CJK** (Type0 with predefined Adobe CMaps — GB1 / CNS1 / Japan1 /
  Korea1) rendered from installed system CJK fonts.
- Honours text rendering modes, including the glyph-clip modes 4–7
  (“draw glyphs as a clip, then paint an image through them”).

### Annotations
- Paints annotation appearance streams — AcroForm field widgets, stamps,
  highlights, free text, etc.

Output: **PNG / JPEG / GIF / BMP / TIFF** (single- and multi-page). Unsupported
operators are skipped, so a page always produces an image.

## Fixed

Driven by visual testing against a real-world PDF corpus (78 fixes). Highlights:

- **Parser robustness** — a direct `/Length` is trusted only when `endstream`
  actually follows it (a bogus `/Length 1` no longer truncates a page); the lexer
  always advances past stray delimiter/binary bytes, so a page whose content fails
  to inflate can no longer spin forever; tolerant xref recovery, object loading, and
  `/Pages` traversal keep partially-damaged files openable; out-of-range
  `startxref`/xref offsets no longer panic; literal-string octal escapes and 40-bit
  RC4 (V=1 R=2) are decoded.
- **Inline images** — accept the ASCIIHex/ASCII85 `>` EOD marker directly before
  `EI`; consume *unfiltered* inline images by exact computed byte length instead of
  scanning for `EI` in binary data; apply the `/DecodeParms` PNG predictor to
  filtered inline images (all three previously corrupted runs of inline-image
  content).
- **Rendering correctness** — text clipping (`Tr` modes 4–7); Separation/DeviceN
  shadings run the tint transform instead of reading one component as gray (no more
  near-black backgrounds); ExtGState constant alpha on images; correct stencil-mask,
  JBIG2 `/Decode` inversion, indexed-palette, and CMYK-JPEG handling.
- **Fonts & text** — render embedded classic Type1; resolve non-embedded CJK to
  installed faces even when the family is installed under a longer name
  (e.g. `Microsoft JhengHei UI`); prefer installed Standard-14 metric-equivalents;
  fill WinAnsi positions 0x80–0x9F in Standard-14 widths. Text **extraction** now
  restores the font and text state on `Q`, fixing labels that decoded through the
  wrong font after a `q … Tf … Q` block.
- **Annotations** — honour gray and CMYK `/IC` interior colours and skip a border
  when no colour is set; correct Line-annotation arrowhead direction and dashing;
  synthesize appearances for Square / Circle / Line / Ink that lack `/AP`; AcroForm
  widget `/AP` matches Acrobat's text layout (no ghosting) and choice fields write
  the `/I` selected-indices array.
- **Showcase** — `docs/feature_showcase.pdf` ships unencrypted so it previews inline
  on GitHub and opens in any viewer.

## Breaking changes

Both are source-incompatible renames; update call sites when upgrading from v0.2.0:

- `(*Page).CropBox` / `TrimBox` / `BleedBox` / `ArtBox` now return a `Rectangle`
  (full box coordinates) instead of a `PageSize`. Use `(*Page).Size()` for
  width/height. (`(*Page).Size()` itself is unchanged.)
- The Info-dictionary API was renamed to mirror Aspose.PDF for .NET:
  `(*Document).Metadata()` → `Info()`, `SetMetadata()` → `SetInfo()`,
  `ClearMetadata()` → `ClearInfo()`, and the `Metadata` struct → `DocumentInfo`.
  (`(*Document).XMP()` remains the XMP store.)

## Out of scope (future)

Deliberately not in v0.3.0 — low real-world frequency or outside the stdlib-only
constraint:

- Mesh shadings (ShadingType 4–7); isolated / knockout transparency groups.
- Non-embedded Symbol glyph shapes and the rarer decorative ZapfDingbats marks.
- Mixed Group 3 2-D fax (`/K > 0`).
- ICCBased profile-aware colour conversion (treated as the underlying device space).
- PDF/A and PDF/UA conformance; digital signatures; RTL / BiDi shaping.

## Fixed

- Type 3 stitching function `/Bounds` now strictly increasing — SVG allows duplicate `<stop offset>` values for sharp color transitions, but the PDF spec (§7.10.4) requires strictly-monotonic bounds. Duplicate offsets are now bumped by a 1e-6 epsilon, preserving visual intent while satisfying the spec. Acrobat previously refused to open documents with non-monotonic bounds.
- SVG group opacity emits `/GSx gs` instead of `//GSx gs` — `ensureExtGState` returns names with a leading slash, so prepending another `/` produced a malformed PDF token that Acrobat rejected with a "document contains errors" warning. Affected SVGs with `<g opacity="...">` children (notably the Aspose logo's highlight-overlay group).

## Out of scope (future)

The following SVG features are deliberately not in v0.2.0 (low real-world frequency or require capabilities outside the stdlib-only constraint):

- `<textPath>` (text along a path), vertical text (`writing-mode`), `xml:space="preserve"`
- `em` / `ex` / `%` length units (require font / parent bbox context)
- `spreadMethod="reflect"` / `"repeat"` (requires PostScript function loops)
- CSS descendant / pseudo / attribute selectors, `<style>` `@media` / `@import`
- True Gaussian blur in `<filter>` (no software rasterizer in stdlib)
- SMIL animation (`<animate>`, `<animateTransform>`)
- External `href` in `<image>` (security + IO surface area)
- `data:image/svg+xml` (recursive parsing)
